$comment: Which browser tests a change needs [scope-33]. Every test carries @component:<name>, @theme:<name> or @sweep (gates/check-tags.mjs refuses one that does not). A changed file is matched against `rules` in order, first match wins; `selectors` turns the rules a stylesheet change touches into components. gates/tags.mjs reads this file; `npm run test:tags` runs what it selects. The measurement against the old selection is under `measured`.

levels.building: the tags of the changed files only, firefox; a theme sweep runs on the three themes below
levels.commit: building plus every @sweep test, firefox; a theme sweep runs on the three themes below
levels.engines: the commit selection in chromium and firefox, at the close of a layer and after a fix to paint, focus or the keyboard [fix-51]; a theme sweep runs on the three themes below
levels.release: every test, chromium and firefox (npm run test:browser), on Kenny's go; a theme sweep runs on all 22
levels.changed: the run before a minor or patch release (npm run test:release, on Kenny's go): the tags of everything changed since the last release tag plus every @sweep test, each sweep on all 22 themes; a major release, or a change the map cannot narrow, runs every test [Kenny, form v9, 2026-10-04]

sweepThemes.$comment: How wide a theme-parameterised sweep runs, per level [scope-103]. gates/run-tags.mjs sets KP_SWEEP_THEMES for the first two levels and nothing for release; tests/helpers/sweep-themes.mjs reads it and answers with every theme when it is unset, so a bare `npx playwright test` still runs all 22. Four theme loops are deliberately NOT narrowed, each with a per-theme fault behind it: focus-visible.spec.mjs (fix-38), registers.spec.mjs:91 (fix-12), reflow.spec.mjs and overflow.spec.mjs (brutalism in firefox only, solstice, and sepia until its removal on 2026-10-08, in chromium only).
sweepThemes.why: the default theme most fixtures and every catalogue page wear, a dark one, and the heaviest register
sweepThemes.measured: 2026-09-16, firefox. The four loops narrowed (fixtures.spec.mjs 6 declarations, surfaces.spec.mjs, concept-confirm.spec.mjs, registers.spec.mjs:187): the whole suite 1593 → 1423 per engine, −170; `--level commit --files css/sepia-register.css` 430 → 266, −164. tests/fixtures.spec.mjs 132 tests in 26.7 s → 18 in 5.4 s; at the release level it is 132 in 25.3 s again.

measured.how: The last 20 commits on round-six that touched css/, js/, components/ or catalogue/ (5e95786 … 6ee15bf), each replayed with `node gates/run-tags.mjs --commit <sha> --dry-run` against the old gates/affected.mjs, counted with `playwright test --list --project=firefox` against the tests of 95dd39b (1251 per engine).
measured.old: affected.mjs said `all` for all 20: every commit touched a stylesheet, a module or a catalogue file, so it ran 1251 tests each time, 25020 in total
measured.building: 9156 in total; 5 of 20 commits still select everything (js/strings.js in four, package.json in one); a catalogue-shell commit selects 47, a formal register commit 157, one catalogue page 63-171
measured.skipped: Every test the old selection ran and the building level does not is a test the map holds uncoupled from the change: catalogue-shell commits skip every test that never opens a catalogue page; a register commit skips the other themes' slices of the sweeps (the commit level runs them) and the tests of components its rules do not name; a catalogue page skips the fixture-page tests of its component. What the map cannot see: a module that fails to load breaks every page that bundles it, and a keyframe name declared in several registers is decided by load order. Both reach far beyond their tags; the commit level's @sweep catches the first on every sweep page, and only the release level catches everything.
measured.commitDuration: Sample 2026-09-14, firefox, 4 workers: tests/registers.spec.mjs (95 @sweep) 32.7 s, tests/fixtures.spec.mjs (132 @sweep) 31.4 s — 227 sweeps in 64 s, so the 352 @sweep tests run in about 100 s and a commit level in about two to three minutes
